LESSON: USES OF DOMESTIC ANIMALS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five
Subject: AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT
Strand: FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested
Topic 2.2: Uses of Domestic animals
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Uses of Domestic animals, part of FOOD PRODUCTION PROCESSES Strand Sub Strand Specific Learning Outcomes Suggested in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade five AGRICULTURE FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How are domestic animals important in food production?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Uses of Domestic animals together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
● Patriotism: The learner appreciates the diversity of animals in their country.

● Respect: The learner develops open mindedness by appreciating diverse opinions from peers as they discuss the uses of different

domestic animals.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Food security: The learner appreciates the importance of animals in terms of food provision.

Link to other subjects:

Science and Technology: The learners apply knowledge of characteristics of animals as living things.

Suggested learning resources:

• Charts on uses of domestic animals in food production.

• Print and non-print media.

• Digital devices.

• Barn.

• Poultry houses
